input: Enroll my parents in a digital literacy workshop

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Digital literacy covers a wide range — email, smartphones, video calls, online safety, social media, etc. Knowing which specific skills to target narrows the search to the right workshop.
Whether the workshop is in-person (and where) or online changes which programs are available and feasible for the parents.
The parents' current comfort level with technology determines whether a beginner, intermediate, or refresher workshop is appropriate.
Budget limits which programs are realistic — some workshops are free (libraries, nonprofits) while others cost money.
Knowing the parents' availability (days, times, duration) is essential for matching them to a workshop schedule they can actually attend.
Language, pace, class size, or instructor style may matter to the parents — e.g., a small group vs. a large class, or a specific language preference.
Understanding what outcome matters most — completing a course, getting a certificate, or simply gaining confidence — shapes which workshop type to prioritize.

gold.taskTitle: Enroll parents in a digital literacy workshop
gold.taskDescription: Find and enroll the user's parents in a suitable digital literacy workshop that matches their needs, location, and skill level.

questions.title: Which specific digital skills do your parents need to learn?
questions.description: Identify the target skill area — e.g., using a smartphone, video calling, email, online safety, social media, or general computer basics.

questions.title: Should the workshop be in-person or online?
questions.description: Determine the format and, if in-person, the city or region where the parents are located.

questions.title: How would you describe your parents' current tech comfort level?
questions.description: Gauge whether they are complete beginners, have some experience, or need a refresher to match them to the right difficulty level.

questions.title: What is your budget for this workshop?
questions.description: Establish whether free options (library programs, nonprofits) are preferred or if paid courses are acceptable.

questions.title: When are your parents available to attend sessions?
questions.description: Capture preferred days, times, and how many weeks or hours they can commit, to filter by schedule compatibility.

questions.title: Do your parents have a preferred language or learning pace?
questions.description: Note any language requirements or preferences for a slow-paced, small-group, or self-directed learning environment.

questions.title: What does a successful outcome look like for your parents?
questions.description: Clarify the end goal — building general confidence, mastering a specific task, or earning a completion certificate — to prioritize the right program.
